correctness.rationale: For smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus g≥2 over algebraically closed characteristic p≥3 admitting a cyclic wild subgroup of exact order N in {2g,2g−1}, Theorem 4.8 of Kazemifard–Tafazolian supplies eight exhaustive normal forms (cited premise, not reproved). For five Artin–Schreier covers of P¹ with r=2,1,4,5,3 distinct poles, Deuring–Shafarevich γ(X)=pγ(base)+(p−1)(r−1) gives 2,0,6,8,8. For remaining three Kummer quotient bases, explicit function-field inverses reduce to v²=u³−u in char3, v²=u³−1 in char5, v²=u⁵−1 in char3. The elliptic Hasse coefficients vanish and the genus-two Hasse–Witt matrix [[0,0],[1,0]] has square zero, so ALL base p-ranks are 0; each Artin–Schreier extension has a single reduced pole and hence rank0. All eight ranks are thus 2,0,6,0,0,0,8,8 in listed order, each either 0 or genus. The char3 genus6 order12 pair has distinct intrinsic rank, so cannot be isomorphic. Independently checked three Kummer identities, two elliptic Hasse coefficients, nilpotent genus-two matrix, eight genus/rank formulas. No claim of Newton polygons or reclassifying the eight cases.

value.rationale: Geometric p-rank is a natural intrinsic Jacobian invariant for a complete, finite, geometrically motivated list of wild cyclic boundary curves; the exact ordinary-versus-zero dichotomy constrains arithmetic moduli behavior and distinguishes two families with the same (p,N,g). The genus-two stable-rank calculation avoids the common error of reading raw Hasse–Witt matrix rank 1 as p-rank 1. Although not a new global curve classification, this is a complete unknown natural invariant for a published classified locus, worthwhile independent of a downstream theorem.
